Rust in one hour

Fast track

Eleven dense lessons for people who already program. Skips the syntax tour and spends the hour on the ownership model, the idioms, the API conventions and the judgement calls that separate working Rust from Rust that fights you.

  • 11 lessons
  • ~61 minutes
  • Experienced in another language, new to Rust.
  • Runs real rustc — no install
Start lesson 1 Open in the app
01

The core model

18 min

The three ideas the rest of Rust is built on, compressed: the mental model, ownership, and types as the design tool.

  1. Rust in five minutes5m The whole language in one annotated program — read this and the rest of the hour is detail.
  2. Ownership, borrowing and lifetimes at speed7m The rules, the four errors you will actually hit, and the decision table for &T vs &mut T vs T.
  3. Types as the design tool6m Making illegal states unrepresentable — the habit that separates Rust that works from Rust that fights you.
02

Writing it idiomatically

18 min

Errors, traits and iterators the way Rust programmers actually write them.

  1. Error handling that scales6m ?, thiserror vs anyhow, adding context, and the honest rules for when to panic.
  2. Traits, generics and dispatch6m Static vs dynamic, the derives you should reach for, and the conversion traits that make APIs pleasant.
  3. Iterators and closures, the idiom6m The chains you will write every day, the Fn traits, and the collect calls you should delete.
03

Engineering decisions

17 min

API design, the concurrency decision tree, and what actually costs performance.

  1. API design and naming conventions6m The conventions the compiler will not teach you, and which the whole ecosystem assumes you know.
  2. The concurrency decision tree6m Threads, rayon, channels, Arc<Mutex> or async — choosing correctly, and why async is often the wrong answer.
  3. Performance: what is free and what is not5m Which abstractions genuinely cost nothing, where the real costs hide, and the five things to check first.
04

Shipping it

8 min

The toolchain you get for free, and the mistakes that cost everyone their first week.

  1. Cargo and the toolchain4m The commands, lints and project hygiene that every Rust codebase assumes.
  2. The mistakes that cost everyone their first week4m Twelve habits from other languages that Rust punishes — and the capstone exercise.

Every lesson here ships with a complete, editable program. Press Run and it is compiled and executed by a real Rust toolchain, so the errors you see are the errors you would get locally.
